questions.q:
What is a constellation?
(A) A single, extremely bright star.
(B) A group of stars that form a pattern when viewed from Earth.
(C) A giant cloud of gas and dust.
(D) A planet that shines at night.
questions.a: (B) is the correct answer. Choosing (A) reveals a misunderstanding that a constellation is a single object, whereas it is actually a collection of many stars.

questions.q: If you draw a line connecting stars to make a "hunter" shape, are those lines actually present in the sky? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, the lines are not in the sky; they are imaginary guides drawn by humans to help us recognize patterns. Answering "yes" suggests a confusion between physical reality and human-made maps.

questions.q: If two stars in a constellation look like they are right next to each other, does that mean they are actually close together in space?
questions.a: No. They only appear close from our perspective on Earth. Thinking they are close ignores the 3D depth of space, where one star might be thousands of times further away than the other.

questions.q: Why do different constellations appear at different times of the year?
questions.a: Because the Earth revolves around the Sun, our perspective of the night sky changes throughout the year. Answering that the stars move themselves shows a misunderstanding of Earth's orbital motion.

questions.q: Could you use the Pole Star to find your direction if you were standing at the South Pole? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, the Pole Star is only visible from the Northern Hemisphere. Claiming you could see it from the South Pole ignores the curvature of the Earth and the specific positioning of stars relative to the Earth's axis.

questions.q: Design a new constellation using five stars in your textbook or a diagram. What would you name it and what story would you tell about it?
questions.a: A good answer creates a unique pattern and links it to a creative, logical story. A poor answer simply picks a random shape without connecting it to a cultural or imaginative narrative.
